text:
Eve: Quick RFC follow-up — which approach do we want for automatic fallback decisioning on canaries: local node-level decisions (probe + degrade locally) or central control-plane decisions? Pros/cons? Want to align before I write the design doc.

Sam: my 2c — local decisions win for latency and isolation. If a rack goes noisy we can fail fast without waiting for control plane. avoids single point of failure.

Priya: central has value though: global correlation, tenant-wide blacklisting, easier to reason about rollbacks across regions. but yeah it adds detection latency and a control-plane availability dependency.

Marco: leaning hybrid. Local for immediate safety (error spike / timeout), central for sustained incidents and cross-tenant policies. local triggers should be conservative to avoid flip-flopping.

Tasha: important: local fallback can break session affinity and KV cache warmups. if node A locally falls back to smaller model variant, its KV cache invalidation might cause downstream latency when it comes back. need a graceful-degrade TTL.

Eve: agreed. concrete proposal: 1) local fast-path: probe + short window (e.g. 10s) error-rate or p95 latency > threshold => local fallback. 2) central coordinator: aggregates 30s signals, can promote a local fallback to global, or veto local undos. 3) policy priorities: tenant-level overrides local if configured.

Sam: sounds good. we should define metric contracts and sampling so local and central use same values. e.g., metrics: inference.errors.total, inference.latency.p95, model.kv.miss_rate.

Priya: +1 on metric names. Also add a heartbeat from local agents so central knows health. but careful about telemetry volume. sample 10% for raw traces, 100% for counters/aggregates.

Marco: pseudo-config idea (sketch):
```yaml
fallback_policies:
  - name: local-fast-fail
    trigger:
      window: 10s
      error_rate_gt: 0.1
      p95_gt_ms: 2000
    action: switch_to_variant: small_model
  - name: central-override
    trigger:
      window: 30s
      aggregated_error_rate_gt: 0.05
    action: promote_global_fallback
```

Tasha: we also need a session-sticky header so clients stay on the same path during a short fallback. maybe set X-Session-Mode: degrade to indicate cache preservation.

Eve: good call. we should define interaction with routing: local fallback should flip a per-instance routing tag but not remove the instance from load balancer unless health-check fails. that avoids capacity oscillation.

Sam: edge case: split-brain where local thinks fallback but central says no. resolution strategy? central should carry higher priority and cause a forced rollback only after a grace window and a higher confidence threshold.

Priya: also consider noisy neighbor: local node error could be due to load spike; fallback to smaller model reduces load but may hide the root cause. central analysis should flag frequent local fallbacks as capacity issues.

Marco: rollout plan suggestion: feature-flag local-fallback on a subset of canaries for 2 weeks at 5% traffic, with autoscrub logs forwarded to a temp index. After stable, enable central aggregation and the promote path.

Tasha: automation hooks for SRE: an oncall playbook that lists how to manually force rollback via control plane (curl example):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://control.redwood.internal/v1/fallbacks/instances/INSTANCE_ID/clear
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment 1765559999 started in us-west-2 (image: canary-2026-03-20).

Eve: next steps — I'll draft a short design doc with: goals, failure modes, policy config, metric contracts, migration plan, and an appendix with playbook commands. any objections to hybrid-first approach?

Sam: nope :thumbsup:

Priya: fine by me, please call out sampling rates and dashboards.

Marco: add a cutover checklist for switching central override live.

Tasha: add cache-preservation rules and session headers.

Eve: great — I'll post the doc tomorrow and tag folks for review. thanks all! :rocket:
